prompt: Use case: precise-object-edit. Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET: a local crop of an accepted dry-bed photograph from a fixed surveillance camera. Image 2 is a LOCATION GUIDE ONLY: the magenta marks the permitted low channel footprint. Change only that guided channel footprint into CLEARLY VISIBLE ORDINARY RUNNING WATER. This must be recognizable flowing water, not a thin blue line and not an extreme flood. Leave exposed dry gravel islands and stones in place. The water surface must be fluid rather than granular mud or solid paste. No uniform yellow/brown/ochre, no tropical blue/green, no transported rocks, no debris masses, debris-flow front, huge waves or excessive whitewater. Retain the original surveillance light, source resolution and camera geometry. The magenta guide is annotation, never a desired output color. Keep exactly the same framing. The stream occupies only the narrow bottom of this deep V-shaped rocky gully. Keep water below the foot of the steep rock walls, visibly following the winding channel from distant upper centre to the foreground lower right. Do not turn the cliff faces into waterfalls. Retain the original individual dry stones at the edges and the unchanged small exposed rock islands. This is ordinary flowing water in a steep gully, with modest irregular white streaks rather than a rolling mud or boulder front.
